Contributing

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Report a reproducible example with the complete specification and package versions. Use synthetic data. Bugs involving threshold boundaries, trust policies, missingness, nonestimable predictions, or audit/provenance records should include a regression test.

Run testthat::test_local() and R CMD check --no-manual after changes. Documentation is generated from roxygen comments. Benchmark changes require a dated plan and a new output directory, including failures, paired baselines and Monte Carlo uncertainty. Do not select a favorable q or data-generating process after inspecting results and then present it as prespecified.

This initial revision used OpenAI Codex for code drafting, literature search, adversarial review, test construction, and simulation orchestration. Runtime validation uses ordinary R code and synthetic data, not an AI model. Human authors retain responsibility for scientific claims, intended-use decisions and release. Versions before 0.4 also used OpenAI Codex. Versions 0.4 and later used Anthropic Claude Code for the same kinds of drafting, search, review and simulation orchestration, and it also wrote most later study plans, decision rules, scoring and write-ups, at the owner’s direction. OpenAI Codex reviewed version 0.7.1 and implemented the three regression fixes and scientific wording corrections in version 0.7.2, including focused tests and release verification. It implemented the pan-backed joint clustered model and its validation in version 0.8.0, with separate AI implementation, mathematical-review and simulation tasks. The write-ups say which rounds, and no independent statistician has reviewed them. Commit trailers record Claude Code’s part, and no AI system is listed as a package or citation author. This is a software assessment and exploratory validation record, not external peer review or a completed manuscript submission certification.
